title: At someone's home
goal: Be a good guest and a good host: arrive, offer and refuse food the polite way, ask 'shall I…?', help with chores, stay the night — and talk about what you used to do.
intro:
Pashtuns are famous for **hospitality** (مېلمستيا): a guest is 'a gift from God', and a host will push food on you until you are truly full. Visiting someone's home has its own little script — take your shoes off at the door, greet the elders first, refuse once or twice before you accept, offer to help even though you know they'll say no.

In this unit you'll learn that script: the words for the home and its chores, how to **offer** and **decline** politely, how to ask **'shall I …?'** with the subjunctive, and how to say what you **used to** do (به + the imperfective past), so you can swap childhood memories with your hosts.

grammar.title: 'Used to': به + the imperfective past
grammar.body:
To talk about things you **used to do** or **would do** regularly in the past, Pashto puts **به** in front of the **imperfective past** (unit 16: the past made from the ordinary, non-و stem, with the stress on the ending):

زه **به** کلي ته **تلم** 'I used to go to the village'
موږ **به** په انګړ کې ويده **کېدو** 'we used to sleep in the courtyard'

Yes, this is the same **به** as the future — the past ending tells you it's a habit, not a future.

The ergative rule still applies to verbs with an object: the doer is oblique (ما، تا، هغه، or a clitic) and the verb agrees with the **object**:
انا **به** مې کيسې **کولې** 'my grandmother used to tell stories' (کيسې f pl)
ما **به** کرکټ **کاوه** 'I used to play cricket' (کرکټ m sg)
پلار **به** مې **ويل** چې … 'my father used to say that …' (no object: m pl)

Useful imperfective pasts of کول: **کاوه** kāwə́ (m sg), **کوله** (f sg), **کول** (m pl), **کولې** (f pl).

**Signals**: پخوا 'in the old days', په ماشومتوب کې 'as a child', هره ورځ / هر کال 'every day / year', کله کله 'sometimes'. For 'not any more' use **نور نه**: اوس نور نه ځم 'I don't go any more'. You can also say **عادت مې و چې …** 'I had a habit of …'.

**The trap**: don't use the perfective (و-) past here — **به** + **وکړل** / **لاړم** means 'would have done' (unit 19), not 'used to'.

grammar.title: 'Shall I …?': the subjunctive as a question
grammar.body:
To offer to do something or to ask what you should do, Pashto simply asks a question with the **subjunctive** — the **perfective present** (unit 10: و- verbs, کړم for کول-compounds, شم for کېدل-compounds):

چای **راوړم**؟ 'Shall I bring tea?'
کړکۍ خلاصه **کړم**؟ 'Shall I open the window?'
زه څه **وکړم**؟ 'What shall I do?'
دلته **کېنم**؟ 'Shall I sit here?'

The person ending tells you who: **وکړو**؟ 'shall we do it?', **راوړي**؟ 'shall he bring it?'.

**Listen for the stress.** For verbs with a prefix (را-، کې-، پرې-) the subjunctive and the ordinary present are spelled the same and differ only in stress: **rāwṛə́m** 'I'm bringing / I'll bring' but **rā́wṛəm** 'shall I bring?'; **kenə́m** 'I sit' but **kénəm** 'shall I sit?'.

For a firmer 'do I have to …?', use **بايد**: بايد بوټونه وباسم؟ 'do I have to take my shoes off?'. The answer to a 'shall I' question is usually an imperative: هو، راوړه! or a polite refusal: نه، زحمت مه کوه.

examples.en: Shall I bring you some water?
Where shall we put the bags?
Do we have to get up early tomorrow?

examples.native: هو، پاتې شه، بړستن درته راوړم.
examples.roman: ho, pā́te sha, baṛastə́n dərta rāwṛə́m.
examples.en: Yes, stay, I'll bring you a quilt.

grammar.title: Offering, accepting and saying no
grammar.body:
In a Pashtun home, offering food is a duty and refusing it is part of the game.

**Offering** — use the **perfective imperative**, and insist: **وخوره** 'eat!', **واخله** 'take some!', **نور واخله** 'have more!', **وڅښه** 'drink!'. To an elder or a guest you've just met use the polite plural: **وخورئ، واخلئ**. **تکلف مه کوه** 'don't be formal' and **دا ستا خپل کور دی** 'this is your own home' are what a host says to make you eat.

**Declining** — never a flat نه. Soften it:
نه، مننه، **موړ يم** 'no thanks, I'm full'
**زحمت مه کوه** 'don't go to any trouble'
**بس دی** 'that's enough'
**په خدای** موړ يم 'honestly (by God), I'm full' — the strongest refusal

**Accepting** — the host will offer again; on the second or third time it is polite to accept a little: ښه، **يوازې لږ** 'OK, just a little'.

**Negative commands** use **مه** + the **imperfective** imperative (no و-): **مه کوه، مه راوړه**. With نه instead of مه the sentence is wrong.

**Leaving** is also negotiated: the guest asks **اجازه راکړئ** 'give me permission (to go)', the host protests **ولې؟ لا وختي دی!** 'why? it's still early!', and only on the second ask lets you go.

examples.roman: dā ham wə́xwrəy, stāso lapā́ra me pox kaṛáy day.
examples.en: Do try this too, I made it for you. (polite)

examples.roman: bas day, nor na shəm xwaṛə́lāy.
examples.en: That's enough, I can't eat any more.
Why? It's still early, sit down!

culture: **Pashtunwali**, the Pashtun code, makes **مېلمستيا** (hospitality) a matter of honour: a host feeds even an enemy who comes as a guest, and a guest is never asked how long they're staying. Shoes come off at the door; meals are eaten sitting on cushions around a **دسترخوان** spread on the floor, with the right hand, and the best pieces of meat are put in front of the guest. Expect to refuse twice and accept on the third offer — a host who only offers once seems stingy, and a guest who accepts at once seems greedy. Men and women usually sit separately when the guests aren't family; in villages male guests are received in the **حجره**, the men's guest house, while female visitors go into the house. A guest asks after 'the people of your house' (د کور خلک) rather than a man's wife by name. Offering to help (مرسته درسره وکړم؟) is polite even though the host will say پرېږده — between close friends of the same age, though, you really are expected to help clear the dastarkhwan. When you leave, ask **اجازه** and expect to be told it's still early.

tip.title: 'Shall I …?' = subjunctive + ?
tip.body:
- Offer or ask with the **perfective present** as a question: چای **راوړم**؟ 'shall I bring tea?', څه **وکړم**؟ 'what shall I do?'.
- Prefix verbs: same spelling, stress on the prefix: **rā́wṛəm** 'shall I bring?' vs rāwṛə́m 'I'm bringing'.
- 'Do I have to …?' = **بايد** + subjunctive: بايد بوټونه وباسو؟

tip.title: Offering and saying no
tip.body:
- Offer with the perfective imperative and insist: **واخله، وخوره، نور واخله** (polite: واخلئ، وخورئ).
- Refuse softly: **موړ يم**، **زحمت مه کوه**، **بس دی**، **په خدای** موړ يم.
- Accept on the second or third offer: **يوازې لږ**.
- 'Don't' = **مه** + imperfective: مه کوه — not نه.

sentences.roman: pə kor ke har tsok yaw kār kawí.
sentences.en: At home everyone has a job to do.

sentences.native: مرسته راسره وکړه، دا ډېر دروند دی.
sentences.roman: mrásta rāsara wə́kṛa, dā ḍer drund day.
sentences.en: Give me a hand, this is really heavy.

sentences.native: ناوخته ده، دلته پاتې شه.
sentences.roman: nāwáxta da, dálta pā́te sha.
sentences.en: It's late, stay here.

sentences.native: بړستن او بالښت درته راوړم.
sentences.roman: baṛastə́n aw bālə́ṣt dərta rāwṛə́m.
sentences.en: I'll bring you a quilt and a pillow.

sentences.native: يوه بله بړستن غواړې؟
sentences.roman: yáwa bə́la baṛastə́n ġwā́ṛe?
sentences.en: Do you want another quilt?

sentences.native: دا بالښت ډېر لوړ دی.
sentences.roman: dā bālə́ṣt ḍer lwaṛ day.
sentences.en: This pillow is too high.

sentences.native: پښتانه ډېر مېلمه پال دي.
sentences.roman: paṣtā́na ḍer melmə́ pāl di.
sentences.en: Pashtuns are very hospitable.

sentences.native: ستا کورنۍ ډېره مېلمه پاله ده.
sentences.roman: stā kornə́y ḍéra melmə́ pā́la da.
sentences.en: Your family is so hospitable.

sentences.native: سهار څو بجې پاڅېږئ؟
sentences.roman: sahā́r tso báje pātséẓəy?
sentences.en: What time do you get up in the morning?

sentences.native: نه، نه، ناوخته نه ده، کېنه!
sentences.roman: na, na, nāwáxta na da, kéna!
sentences.en: No, no, it's not late, sit down!

sentences.native: سبا وختي کار لرم.
sentences.roman: sabā́ waxtí kār lárəm.
sentences.en: I have work early tomorrow.

sentences.native: ستا کور ته به بيا راشم.
sentences.roman: stā kor ta ba biyā́ rā́shəm.
sentences.en: I'll come to your place again.

lessons.title: When I was a kid …

tip.title: 'Used to': به + imperfective past
tip.body:
- **به** + imperfective past (no و-) = a past habit: زه **به** کلي ته **تلم** 'I used to go to the village'.
- Transitive verbs stay ergative: انا **به** مې کيسې **کولې** (agrees with کيسې).
- کول: کاوه (m) · کوله (f) · کول (m pl) · کولې (f pl).
- 'Not any more' = **نور نه**.

new: پخوا به موږ هره جمعه دلته راتلو.

sentences.native: په ماشومتوب کې به مې ډېرې لوبې کولې.
sentences.roman: pə māshumtób ke ba me ḍére lóbe kawə́le.
sentences.en: As a child I used to play a lot.

sentences.native: هر اوړي به موږ کلي ته تلو.
sentences.roman: har oṛí ba muẓ kə́li ta tlu.
sentences.en: Every summer we used to go to the village.

sentences.native: انا به مې هره شپه کيسې کولې.
sentences.roman: anā́ ba me hára shpa kissé kawə́le.
sentences.en: My grandmother used to tell stories every night.

sentences.native: پخوا به زه ډېر ناوخته ويده کېدم.
sentences.roman: pəxwā́ ba zə ḍer nāwáxta widə́ kedə́m.
sentences.en: I used to go to sleep really late.

sentences.native: په ماشومتوب کې به موږ په يوه کوټه کې ويده کېدو.
sentences.roman: pə māshumtób ke ba muẓ pə yawa kóṭa ke widə́ kedú.
sentences.en: As kids we used to sleep in one room.

sentences.native: پلار به مې ويل چې کار تر هر څه مخکې دی.
sentences.roman: plār ba me wayə́l che kār tər har tsə mə́xke day.
sentences.en: My father used to say that work comes before everything.

sentences.native: هغه به هره ورځ ما ته زنګ واهه.
sentences.roman: haġə́ ba hára wradz mā ta zang wāhə́.
sentences.en: He used to call me every day.

sentences.native: پخوا مې دا عادت نه و.
sentences.roman: pəxwā́ me dā ādát na wə.
sentences.en: I didn't use to have this habit.

sentences.native: زما عادت دی چې سهار وختي پاڅېږم.
sentences.roman: zmā ādát day che sahā́r waxtí pā́tseẓəm.
sentences.en: I'm in the habit of getting up early.

sentences.native: زموږ پخوانی کور ډېر لوی و.
sentences.roman: zmuẓ pəxwānáy kor ḍer loy wə.
sentences.en: Our old house was really big.

sentences.native: اوس نور هلته نه ځو.
sentences.roman: os nor hálta na dzu.
sentences.en: We don't go there any more.

sentences.native: کله کله اوس هم هغه کلي ته ځم.
sentences.roman: kə́la kə́la os ham haġə́ kə́li ta dzəm.
sentences.en: Sometimes I still go to that village.
